issues.title: Cross-field validation uses field validator
issues.description: The rule requires cross-field validation to use @model_validator decorator, but the code uses @field_validator which accesses unvalidated fields via info.data, causing order-dependent validation issues
issues.rule_name: Pydantic Models Must Use model_validator for Cross-Field Validation

issues.title: Incorrect automation_triggered_event_id for state-specific actions
issues.description: When actions_on_trigger or actions_on_resolve are executed, they should be linked to their specific triggered_event.id or resolved_event.id respectively. However, the code incorrectly uses primary_state_change_event_id (which always prefers Triggered over Resolved) for both types of actions. This breaks the tracing chain for actions_on_resolve - they will reference the wrong event ID when only a Resolved state change occurs, making it impossible to correctly trace the action back to the automation.resolved event that actually prompted it.

issues.title: Missing related resources in action.triggered event on failure path
issues.description: In the fail() method, the code builds related_resources list that includes both automation-triggered-event and triggering-event references. However, when emitting the 'prefect.automation.action.triggered' event, it incorrectly uses self._resulting_related_resources instead of the newly built related_resources list. This means the action.triggered event will not include the automation-triggered-event or triggering-event links on the failure path, breaking the traceability chain documented in the PR. Users won't be able to trace from failed actions back to their source events.

issues.title: Validation incorrectly rejects proactive triggers with automation_triggered_event_id
issues.description: The field_validator for automation_triggered_event_id prevents setting this field when triggering_event is None. However, proactive triggers (which have no triggering_event) still create automation.triggered events and need to link actions to them via automation_triggered_event_id. The code in triggers.py sets automation_triggered_event_id=primary_state_change_event_id for all actions including proactive triggers, causing Pydantic validation to fail at runtime. This breaks all proactive automations, which is a critical functional regression.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #20227 - Link automation.action.* events to automation.triggered event
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds an `automation_triggered_event_id` field to `TriggeredAction`, populates it in `triggers.act()` with the ID of the `automation.triggered` (or `automation.resolved`) state-change event, and adds an `automation-triggered-event` related resource to `automation.action.*` events. It also adds a `triggering-event` related resource to the `executed`/`failed` events in `succeed()`/`fail()`, and consolidates duplicated `Resource` construction in `succeed()`. The goal (traceability from `action.failed` back to the trigger) is sound, and the test updates are broad.

Reading the head code, I found two real defects. First, the new validator on `automation_triggered_event_id` rejects any non-None ID when `triggering_event` is None. Proactive firings can legitimately have `triggering_event=None` (`triggering_event or bucket.last_event`, and absence-style buckets start with `last_event=None`), but `act()` still passes the Triggered state-change ID to them. That makes `TriggeredAction(...)` raise `ValidationError` inside `act()`, so the action is never published. Second, in `fail()` the `action.triggered` event was switched to `related=self._resulting_related_resources`, which drops both the `triggering-event` and the new `automation-triggered-event` links from that event, while `succeed()` keeps them. The new tests that assert those links on the triggered event will fail.

I could not execute the test suite here: the hosted-API fixture times out in this environment, so the failure claims are from reading the code, not from a passing/failing run. Both are small fixes, but the validator issue would break proactive automations at runtime, so I'd block the merge on it.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The validator makes `TriggeredAction` construction fail for proactive firings with no triggering event, which stops those automations' actions from being published. The `fail()` change silently removes the new trace links and the pre-existing triggering-event link from `action.triggered`, and the updated tests for that path will fail. Both need fixing before merge.

architecture.overview:
Automations are evaluated by the triggers service (`src/prefect/server/events/triggers.py`). When a trigger fires, `fire()` calls `act()`, which publishes the `prefect.automation.triggered` / `resolved` state-change events and then creates one `TriggeredAction` per configured action. Each `TriggeredAction` is published as a message to the actions service, which runs the action (`Action.act`) and then calls `Action.succeed()` or `Action.fail()` in `src/prefect/server/events/actions.py`. Those methods emit `prefect.automation.action.triggered` and then `executed` or `failed` events, with related resources pointing at the triggering event and, until now, nothing that links back to the state-change event.

This PR threads the state-change event ID through the pipeline. `act()` picks the Triggered event (falling back to Resolved) and stores its ID on each `TriggeredAction` in a new `automation_triggered_event_id` field. The actions service then adds an `automation-triggered-event` related resource to the action events. It also adds a `triggering-event` link to `executed`/`succeeded` events and makes `succeed()` reuse the same `resource` object instead of rebuilding it. The `fail()` path is where the wiring goes wrong: the `action.triggered` event loses both links.
steps: Entry point: the triggers service's `fire()` (triggers.py) calls `act(firing)`, which publishes state-change events and builds one `TriggeredAction` per action.

New linkage in `act()`: the primary state-change event ID (Triggered preferred over Resolved) is passed as `automation_triggered_event_id` into each `TriggeredAction`. The new field and its validator are in `schemas/automations.py`, and the validator is where the proactive-trigger crash originates.

Actions service: `Action.fail()` and `Action.succeed()` in actions.py build `related_resources` with the new `automation-triggered-event` link and the existing `triggering-event` link. `fail()` emits its triggered event with the wrong list (`_resulting_related_resources`), which is the second defect.
Docs: `docs/v3/concepts/automations.mdx` documents the two related-resource roles and the event names, which matches the intended design but not the current `fail()` behaviour.

findings.title: Proactive automations crash in act() because of the new validator
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/server/events/schemas/automations.py`, the `TriggeredAction` field validator `validate_automation_triggered_event_id` (around lines 772-780) raises when `automation_triggered_event_id` is set but `triggering_event` is None. That breaks proactive firings, where `act()` in `triggers.py` correctly sets the ID but the firing has no triggering event, so `TriggeredAction` construction raises and the action is never published. Remove this validator. The link to `automation.triggered` doesn't depend on `triggering_event`. Keep the `automation_triggered_event_id` field itself. Then confirm `test_acting_publishes_an_action_message_from_a_proactive_trigger` in `tests/events/server/triggers/test_service.py` passes, and consider adding a test that a proactive firing with `triggering_event=None` still produces an action carrying `automation_triggered_event_id`.

findings.title: action.triggered event drops the new and existing trigger links in fail()
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/server/events/actions.py`, `Action.fail()` emits the `prefect.automation.action.triggered` event with `related=self._resulting_related_resources` (around line 202). Change it to `related=related_resources` so the triggered event carries the `automation-triggered-event` and `triggering-event` links, matching `succeed()`. Leave the `action.failed` event as it is. Then run `tests/events/server/actions/test_actions_service.py`, in particular `test_failure_events_include_automation_triggered_event_link` and `test_action_events_without_automation_triggered_event_id`.

findings.title: Duplicated related-resource block in fail() and succeed()
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/server/events/actions.py`, `Action.fail()` and `Action.succeed()` each build the same `related_resources` list: the resulting related resources, then `automation-triggered-event` if `automation_triggered_event_id` is set, then `triggering-event` if `triggering_event` is set. Extract this into a private helper on `Action` (for example `_build_related_resources(triggered_action)`) and call it from both methods. Keep the `related=` argument for each emitted event unchanged. Don't change any event payloads or ordering.

findings.title: actions_on_resolve actions link to the Triggered event even when Resolved fired
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/server/events/triggers.py`, `act()` assigns `primary_state_change_event_id` (Triggered preferred over Resolved) to every `source_actions` tuple, including the `actions_on_resolve` entries. Those actions are prompted by the Resolved event, so their `automation_triggered_event_id` should be the Resolved state-change event's ID. Change the `actions_on_resolve` tuple to use `state_change_events[TriggerState.Resolved].id`, and keep Triggered preference only for the default and `actions_on_trigger` cases. Confirm the docs in `docs/v3/concepts/automations.mdx` still match.

findings.title: Existing action-event tests were updated to match the new related resources
findings.body:
The PR updates every action test that asserted on `related` (executing, failing, pausing, resuming, notification, webhook, and others) to expect the new `triggering-event` link. Those are mechanical, consistent updates, and they make the behaviour change explicit rather than hiding it. The new tests for the trigger-link path also check both the triggered and executed or failed events, which is the right granularity for this feature.

The tests are also a good demonstration of why the `fail()` path matters: the `action.triggered` assertions would have caught the list swap if they had been run against the failing branch.

findings.title: Docs describe the new related-resource roles clearly
findings.body: The new section in `docs/v3/concepts/automations.mdx` lists the two related-resource roles and explains the causal chain from `action.failed` back to the trigger. That is useful for operators debugging automation failures, and it documents the event names users will see. Once the `fail()` and proactive-trigger issues above are fixed, the docs will match the behaviour.
